title: Sabalenka, Rybakina handed shock defeats at China  Open tennis | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:38
-     - 0

Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open, leaving the event without its top two seeds as world number one Elena Rybakina was ousted in the second round.

Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes yesterday.

Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.

Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.

The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Elena Rybakina – who replaced Sabalenka as the world number one last month – was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round.

Top seed Alexander Zverev was scheduled to play Novak Djokovic later yesterday in the quarter-finals of the men’s 500-level event also taking place.

The 39-year-old Serbian great enters the match with an extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing, but Zverev — last month’s US Open champion — is in the running for the top men’s ranking.

title: Red Bull’s Verstappen wins rain-delayed Bahrain GP F1 race in Sepang | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:37
-     - 0

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen has finally won his first race of the Formula One season amid chaotic scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was held in Malaysia an hour and 40 minutes late due to heavy rain.

Verstappen gained the lead yesterday after an early safety car and led home the Mercedes of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in second and the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton in third at the Sepang International Circuit.

But there was agony for George Russell, who had to retire from third place in the second Mercedes with five laps to go when his power unit appeared to fail under a late safety car.

Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the F1 calendar, and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red ‌‌Bull a huge boost despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one.

Hamilton started on the front row on dry tyres and quickly slid down the field in the wet conditions.

But the seven-time world champion used all his experience to work his way back through the field for a brilliant podium place as the surface dried out.

His teammate Charles Leclerc was fourth with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar in fifth.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was raced in Malaysia due to the US-Israel war on Iran, which has caused disruptions to the international sports calendar.

Formula One moves on to nearby Singapore for a night race and sprint this weekend.

title: DFCC Bank athletes shine at 41st Annual Mercantile Athletics Championships 2026 | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:36
-     - 0

DFCC Bank’s Athletics Team delivered an impressive performance at the 41st Annual Mercantile Athletics Championships 2026, securing a total of 15 medals – five gold, two silver and eight bronze – across a range of track and field events.

The three-day championship, held from 21 to 23 August 2026 at the Mahinda Rajapaksa Stadium, brought together nearly 1,800 athletes representing 46 companies from Sri Lanka’s mercantile sector, providing a competitive platform for athletes to demonstrate their sporting talent and determination.

Among DFCC Bank’s standout performers was Chanidu Senash, who claimed two gold medals in the Novices Men’s category, winning both the 110m Hurdles and Triple Jump. He also secured fifth place in the Long Jump.

Ruwan Madushanka added two more gold medals to DFCC Bank’s tally in the Men’s 35+ category, taking first place in both the 400m and 1,500m Race Walk, while also securing bronze in the 400m Hurdles.

Continuing the Bank’s strong showing, Sahan Rodrigo won gold in the Men’s 40+ High Jump and secured bronze in Shot Put. Kalpani Wasalage earned two silver medals in the Women’s 30+ category in Discus Throw and Javelin Throw, while finishing fourth in Shot Put.

DFCC Bank athletes also delivered several notable bronze-medal performances. Geemali Athukorala secured bronze in both Javelin Throw and Shot Put in the Women’s 30+ category, while Nirasha Madakumbura won bronze in Hammer Throw and Shot Put in the Novices Women’s category. Zamri Hayauddin secured bronze in the Men’s 30+ Triple Jump, while Dumith Samarathunga earned bronze in the Men’s 30+ Javelin Throw.

Beyond the medal-winning performances, several other members of Team DFCC achieved strong placements across individual and relay events, reflecting the depth of talent within the Bank’s athletics team. Athletes competed across sprinting, jumping, throwing, race walking and relay events, demonstrating commitment, teamwork and competitive spirit throughout the championship.

The achievements at the 41st Annual Mercantile Athletics Championships reflect DFCC Bank’s commitment to encouraging employees to pursue excellence beyond the workplace and maintain an active and well-rounded lifestyle.

title: After Asian Games Gold, another honour for Rumesh Tharanga | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:34
-     - 0

Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage (right) receives his promotion to the rank of Sergeant following his historic Gold-medal victory at the 2026 Commonwealth Games

By Hishan Welmilla

With Sri Lanka Air Force Sergeant Rumesh Tharanga writing another golden chapter in the country’s sporting history, the time may have come for the Sri Lanka Air Force to consider whether his latest achievement deserves another special honour or official promotion.

An Air Force athlete, Rumesh Tharanga previously won the men’s javelin throw gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. In recognition of that international achievement, he was promoted from the rank of Corporal to Sergeant. The promotion was granted by the Commander of the Air Force as recognition of his outstanding contribution to Sri Lanka through sport.

But Rumesh did not stop there.

At the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, Tharanga produced another historic performance, winning the men’s javelin throw gold medal with a distance of 88.55 metres. In doing so, he became the first Sri Lankan to win an Asian Games gold medal in the men’s javelin throw.

It was not simply another medal.

It was a landmark achievement for Sri Lankan athletics.

Winning both Commonwealth Games and Asian Games gold medals in the same year has placed Rumesh Tharanga among the country’s most successful athletes on the international stage. His performances at Diamond League competitions have also demonstrated his ability to compete against the world’s leading javelin throwers. In June 2026, the Sri Lanka Air Force itself described him as the world’s No. 2 ranked men’s javelin thrower.

The question, therefore, is no longer simply whether Rumesh Tharanga has won another medal.

He has created history for Sri Lanka — while wearing the uniform of the Sri Lanka Air Force.

That raises a legitimate question: following the promotion he received after his Commonwealth Games gold medal, should the Air Force now consider another special promotion or official honour in recognition of his Asian Games gold medal and his continued international success?

There is already an institutional precedent.

Sri Lanka Air Force Corporal Dulith Dasanayake was promoted to the rank of Sergeant in recognition of an outstanding international achievement after winning gold and setting a new world record at the World Strength Lifting Championships. His promotion represented an important example of how the institution can recognise an athlete who brings distinction to Sri Lanka on the international stage.

Rumesh Tharanga has now become another exceptional chapter in that story.

The Air Force has already recognised Rumesh’s achievements.

The question now is whether that recognition should be taken one step further following his historic Asian Games gold medal.

Considering his latest achievement, his sustained performances at the highest levels of international athletics and his contribution to Sri Lankan sport, the relevant authorities of the Sri Lanka Air Force could consider whether he deserves an appropriate further promotion or special official recognition, in keeping with the precedent established through the recognition of athletes such as Dulith Dasanayake.

For the next generation of Sri Lankan athletes, perhaps the most powerful message would be a simple one: Win for your country. Your country will not forget you.

title: Karma Fight League expands to India, Pakistan and Nepal as KFL 9 puts Colombo on world stage | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:33
-     - 0

India’s Fahad Zedan celebrates his championship win at KFL 9 held on 12 September at Sri Lanka Exhibition and Convention Centre

Karma Fight League (KFL), Sri Lanka’s largest combat sports property, is taking its business beyond the island. The league will roll out Road to KFL (RKFL), its amateur qualifying series, in India, Pakistan and Nepal in November and December 2026.

The expansion follows nine successful events in Colombo, the latest being KFL 9 on 12 September, at the Sri Lanka Exhibition and Convention Centre (SLECC). All nine bouts on the card were international match-ups, featuring athletes from Sri Lanka, India, Pakistan and Nepal, including two women’s contests. Over 3,000 fans attended live, while hundreds of thousands more followed the event digitally.

In the main event, India’s Fahad Zedan defeated Sri Lanka’s Januka Ranaweera to become the KFL World Light Welterweight Champion. He is the league’s third title holder, after Sri Lanka’s Kavindu Rasanjaya and India’s Sonam Zomba, who is ranked South Asia’s number one female fighter.

Karma Fight League Chairman Raveen Wickramasinghe said: “KFL’s future is regional. Road to KFL takes us into India, Pakistan and Nepal, and from there we build a South Asian combat sports platform that the world pays attention to.”

Corporate backing has followed. Ruhunu Hospital, the largest private healthcare provider in the Southern Province, was title sponsor of KFL 9 under a multi-event partnership that also covers athlete medical support and event safety.

Ruhunu Hospital Assistant Medical Director Dr. Hasara Kulatunga said: “Ruhunu Hospital has built its reputation on clinical standards, and we believe those standards belong in sport too. Working with KFL allows us to contribute to the development of combat sports in Sri Lanka and to give athletes a professional environment with the right medical cover. As the league takes its qualifiers across South Asia, we look forward to seeing more athletes benefit.” 

KFL 9 was endorsed by Sri Lanka Tourism and the Ministry of Tourism, reflecting the country’s push to position itself as a regional destination for sport and entertainment. Events of this scale bring athletes, officials and supporters from neighbouring countries to Colombo.

KFL is planning a larger KFL 10 and further expansion in 2027.

title: St. Benedict’s College shines at Sir John Tarbat Senior Athletics Championship 2026 | Daily FT

St. Benedict’s College, Colombo 13, produced an impressive performance at the Sir John Tarbat Senior Athletics Championship 2026, securing runners-up positions in the Overall Track Events and Overall Relay, while finishing as the 2nd Runners-up in the Overall Championship.

The Benedictine athletes displayed determination, discipline and fighting spirit throughout the championship, delivering a series of strong performances on the track and field.

A major highlight of the meet was the outstanding performance of Sasindu Hansana Jayasinghe, who was named the Most Outstanding Athlete of the Meet for his exceptional achievements.

Sasindu’s success reflects six years of dedicated training and development. His remarkable journey has seen him progress from a 4-metre long jump to an outstanding 16.23m triple jump, marking a significant achievement in his athletics career and highlighting the growing strength of Benedictine athletics.

His performance was also a proud moment for the school’s athletics program, with the coaching team continuing its commitment to developing athletes capable of competing at the highest level.

The school expressed its appreciation to Jumping Specialist Ravindra Weerakkody and the entire coaching and support team for their dedication and contribution to the athletes’ success.

Despite the challenges faced throughout the championship, the Benedictine athletes remained focused on their goals and responded with determination and commitment on the track.

The impressive results at the Sir John Tarbat Senior Athletics Championship 2026 underline the continued progress of St. Benedict’s College athletics and provide further motivation for the team as it looks ahead to its next challenge.

title: People’s Bank powers national U20 School Basketball Championship | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:30
-     - 0

People’s Bank is powering the Inter-School Under-20 Basketball Championship 2026, supporting the development of young sporting talent as the national school basketball tournament got underway on 1 October.

The championship was announced at a special media conference held recently at the Language Hall of Nalanda College, Colombo 10, attended by the Sri Lanka Schools Basketball Association President Iran Champika Silva, officials of People’s Bank and the Association, and student athletes.

The tournament will provide a competitive national platform for young basketball players to demonstrate their skills, determination and sportsmanship while gaining valuable experience through high-level inter-school competition.

A total of 60 boys’ teams will compete in Divisions A, B and C, with Division C Comprising Tier 1 and Tier 2. The girls’ competition will feature 26 teams competing in Divisions A, B Tier 1, B Tier 2, C Tier 1 and C Tier 2.

The final-stage matches will be held from 9 to 12 November at the Sugathadasa Stadium, Colombo, culminating in the awards ceremony on 12 November at 5.30 p.m.

Through its partnership with the championship, People’s Bank continues to support the growth of school sports and provide opportunities for the country’s young athletes to develop their talent and pursue sporting excellence.

title: South Africa’s Pretorius smashes Gayle’s T20 cricket record score | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:15
-     - 0

Lhuan-dre Pretorius

Lhuan-dre Pretorius hit 188* off 79 deliveries in Bloemfontein to break Chris Gayle’s record score in the T20 format.

Playing for the Titans against the Knights in the South African CSA Challenge, the 20-year-old left-hander opened the batting and hit 13 sixes and 14 fours in his innings to surpass Gayle’s 175 for Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League in 2013.

Pretorius reached 50 in 24 balls, needed 16 more to get to his century and took another 18 to hit 150.

Gayle scored his 175 off 66 balls, striking 17 sixes and 13 fours.

The 20-year-old has represented South Africa in all three international formats. He was making his first Titans appearance of the season after scoring 226 total runs, tied for most with Dewald Brevis, in a three-nation series in Namibia in September.

The second-highest scorer was Sinethemba Qeshile with 14 as the Titans finished on 267-3.

They then bowled out the Knights for 143 to win by 124 runs.

title: West Indies beat India in record chase as Hope hits 162 in third ODI | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 5 October 2026 02:14
-     - 0

Captain Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 led West Indies to a record run-chase win against India in one-day international cricket in Chandigarh.

The West Indies achieved their highest ODI run chase on Saturday, reaching 352-5 and winning by five wickets with 10 balls to spare after India made 351-7, featuring Lokesh Rahul’s 129.*

India had already won the three-match series after eight-wicket wins in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati. But the West Indies, chasing for the first time in the series, overcame India for the first time since 2023.

Hope promoted himself to opening batter after Jewel Andrew reportedly injured a finger making a catch and had to go to hospital. After keeping wicket for all of India’s 50 overs in high humidity, he batted brilliantly to score his second successive hundred in the series but struggled in the last overs.

Fittingly, he hit the winning run.

His second-highest ODI score, from 143 balls, included 17 boundaries and three sixes. Amir Jangoo added 67 off 56 and Keemo Paul 44 off 35.

The teams begin a five-match Twenty20 series tomorrow (6), starting in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
